
# Getting started {#sec-getting_started}

This chapter will get your computer set up with what you need for the course. You need to read carefully and follow instructions to the letter. They are different on Mac and Windows so pick which kind of computer you have below:

::: {.panel-tabset group="platform"}

## <i class="bi bi-apple"></i> Mac

**1.** Quit VS Code completely first if it is running. 

**2.** Open a new Terminal window and run this command to download the course folder

```bash
curl https://munch-group.org/instructing-machines/instructing-machines.zip > ~/Downloads/instructing-machines.zip
```

**3.** Run this to unpack the student folder and put it in your home folder:

```bash
unzip -o ~/Downloads/instructing-machines.zip && mv ~/Downloads/instructing-machines ~/.
```

**4.** Navigate to the course folder

```bash
cd ~/instructing-machines
```

**5.** Run this to install Pixi

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | SHELL="$(ps -o comm= -p $$ | sed 's/^-//')" sh
```

**6.** Run this to make sure you can use pixi from the terminal;

```bash
pixi run shell
```

**7.** Now quit that Terminal *completely* and open a new one. 

**8.** Run this in the new terminal to make sure pixi is installed. If it is, it will print its version nr.

```bash
pixi --version
```

**9.** Run this to build the environment:

```bash
pixi clean ; pixi install
```

**10.** Finish the setup 

```bash
pixi run check
```
<!-- 
for 2027

```bash
pixi run setup
``` 
-->

**11.** Install the course tool

```bash
pixi global install -c conda-forge -c munch-group im-course-tools
```


## <i class="bi bi-windows"></i> Windows


**1.** Quit VS Code completely first if it is running. 

**2.** Open a new PowerShell (Start menu → PowerShell) and run this command to download the course folder.

```bash
iwr -Uri "https://munch-group.org/instructing-machines/instructing-machines.zip" -OutFile "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\instructing-machines.zip"
```

**3.** Run this to unpack the student folder and put it in your home folder:

```txt
Expand-Archive -Path "$HOME\Downloads\instructing-machines.zip" -DestinationPath C:\
```

**4.** Navigate to the course folder

```
cd C:\instructing-machines
```

**5.** Run this to install Pixi

```txt
irm -useb https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex
```

**6.** Run this to make sure you can use pixi from Powershell;

```
pixi run shell
```

**7.** Now quit that Powershell *completely* and open a new one. 

**8.** Run this in the new Powershell to make sure pixi is installed. If it is, it will print its version nr.

```
pixi --version
```

**9.** Run this to build the environment:

```
pixi clean ; pixi install
```

**10.** Finish the setup 

```
pixi run check
```
<!-- 
for 2027

```
pixi run setup
``` 
-->

**11.**  Install the course tool

```
pixi global install -c conda-forge -c munch-group im-course-tools
```

:::

::: {.callout-note}

If `pixi install` fails, it may be because you have antivirus software (other than Microsoft Defender) that blocks Pixi from downloading packages. Here are instructions for how do do this for: [BitDefender](https://www.bitdefender.com/consumer/support/answer/13425/), [Norton](https://knowledge.civilgeo.com/adding-an-exception-to-norton-firewall), [McAfee](https://knowledge.civilgeo.com/adding-an-exception-to-mcafee-firewall), [Kaspersky](https://knowledge.civilgeo.com/adding-an-exception-to-kaspersky-firewall).

:::


## The VScode editor {#sec-text-editor}

You will also need a *text editor*. A text editor is where you write your Python code. For this course, we will use *Visual Studio Code* — or *VS Code* for short. You can download it from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/download). If you open VS Code, you should see something like @fig-vscode.

You may wonder why we cannot use Word to create and edit files with programming code. The reason is that a text editor made for programming, such as VS Code, only saves the actual characters you type. So, unlike Word, it does not silently save all kinds of formatting, like margins, boldface text, headers, etc. With VS Code, what you type is *exactly* what is in the file when you save it. In addition, where Word is made for prose, VS Code is made for programming and has many features that will make your programming life easier.

![Visual Studio Code](./images/vscode.png){#fig-vscode width=80%}

**1.** If VS Code was already running, quit it completely and start it again before you go on. Not "close the window", quit the application. 

**1.** Open VS Code. The first time you start VS Code it greets you with a welcome screen that wants you to sign in. Nothing on this course needs an account, so click **Continue without signing in**.

**2.** Open the `instructing-machines` folder using `File → Open Folder`. The entire setup only works if you open the *folder*. If you just open any single file **nothing will work**.

**3.** Accept when prompted to trust and install recommended extensions. If asked to trust the folder/workspace, accept that too. If there is a blue button saying "Trust" at the bottom left, click that too. 




## Opening a folder in VS Code from the terminal

Once you have VS Code installed, there is an alternative way to open a folder directly from the terminal. In a terminal, `cd` into the course folder and then run `code .`. `.` means "the current folder".

```bash
code .
```

On Windows this works straight away, but on a Mac you need to do the following to make the `code` command available. Close all your Terminal windows. In VS Code, press `Cmd+Shift+P`, type `Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH`, and press Enter.

## If something goes wrong {#sec-if-something-goes-wrong}

- **"pixi is not recognized as an internal or external command" (Windows).** The terminal you are typing in was opened before pixi was installed. Close it and open a new one. If you are inside VS Code, quit VS Code entirely and start it again.
- **"command not found: pixi" (Mac).** The terminal you are typing in was opened before pixi was installed. Close it and open a new one. If you are inside VS Code, quit VS Code entirely and start it again.
- **Windows says a script cannot be run, or mentions an execution policy.** You have found a PowerShell install script somewhere. Do not fight with it — use the `.msi` installer linked in [Installing pixi](#sec-installing-pixi) instead. It needs no permissions of that kind.
- **`pixi install` fails part-way, or complains about paths being too long.** The folder is almost certainly too deep, or inside OneDrive. Move the whole folder to `C:\bioprog\` and run `pixi install` again.
- **The window still says *Restricted Mode*, or nothing Python-related works at all.** The folder is untrusted, which is how VS Code opens every new folder now, and extensions do not run until you change it. Click the blue **Restricted Mode** button in the bottom left corner, then **Trust** ([Opening the folder](#sec-opening-the-folder), step 2). Then reload the window, because the extensions have been sitting switched off until this moment.
- **"No Python found. Would you like to install uv and use it to install Python?"** Say no. You have a Python already — it is in the `.pixi` folder, and this message means VS Code has not found it rather than that it is missing. The usual cause is a VS Code that was started before pixi was installed: quit VS Code completely, start it again, and open the folder. If it persists, see the next entry.
- **A warning about a "default environment manager" that "is not registered".** Ignore it. Two extensions start at the same time and one of them reads a setting a fraction of a second before the other is ready to answer; a moment later it is. Nothing is broken, and there is nothing for you to do. We would silence it if we could, but the setting it is complaining about is the one that gives your kernel its name.
- **The pixi extension really does do nothing — no `Instructing Machines` anywhere, and no `.pixi` path offered.** This is different from the warning above. The extension has to run the `pixi` command before it can find anything, and it cannot. `pixi run check` writes the full path to pixi into the folder's settings for exactly this reason, so run it if you have not, and reload the window. If you have run it and nothing changes, you have probably copied this folder from a different computer, where that path pointed somewhere that does not exist here: run `pixi run check` again to rewrite it for this machine.
- **There is no `Instructing Machines` entry in the kernel list.** It is created by `pixi run check`, so run that first if you have not. If it is still missing, make sure you opened the *folder* ([Opening the folder](#sec-opening-the-folder)), that `pixi install` has finished, and that the recommended extensions are installed. Then run `Developer: Reload Window` from the command palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`, or `Cmd+Shift+P` on a Mac), which makes VS Code look again.
- **A widget shows as blank space, or as raw text.** You are running the notebook on the wrong Python. Click `Select Kernel` in the top right of the notebook and choose the one whose path contains `.pixi`.
- **Nothing works and the lecture has already started.** Open the course website and use the in-browser notebooks. They run Python inside the browser with nothing installed, they are slower and slightly limited, and they will get you through the next hour. ## Safe procedure on Windows {#sec-safe-windows-procedure}

1. Quit VS Code completely first if it is running. 

2. Then in PowerShell (Start menu → PowerShell, not VS Code's terminal):

```txt
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm -useb https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex"
```

3. Now close that terminal *completely* and open a new one. 

4. Run this in the new terminal to make sure pixi is installed. If it is, it will print its version nr.

```txt
pixi --version
```

5. Run this in the terminal and answer `Y` when prompted.

```txt
Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
```

6. Delete any instructing-machines.zip files in your Downloads folder

7. To to the "getting started" and download the course folder again.

8. Run this to unpack the course folder in a place Windows will not fight you

```txt
Expand-Archive -Path "$HOME\Downloads\instructing-machines.zip" -DestinationPath C:\im
```

9. Run this to navigate to the course-folder

```txt
cd C:\im\instructing-machines
```

10. Run this to build the environment:

```txt
pixi clean ; pixi install
```

11. Finish the setup 

```txt
pixi run setup
```

Install the course tool

```txt
pixi global install -c conda-forge -c munch-group im-course-tools
```

12. Then open C:\im\instructing-machines in VS Code using `File → Open Folder`.

Well done! You are all set to start the course. Have a cup of coffee, and look forward to your first program.
